hints: Look carefully at the table and pick out just the two numbers you need: the starting pressure in the arteriole (11.3 kPa) and the finishing pressure at the arterial end of the capillary (4.7 kPa).
Remember percentage decrease always uses the starting value on the bottom: (starting value minus finishing value) divided by starting value, then times 100.
walkthrough:
**Pick out the start and finish pressures**

Blood flows from arteriole to capillary, so we start high and end low.

Start = $11.3 \text{ kPa}$, Finish = $4.7 \text{ kPa}$.

**Find the actual drop in pressure**

Subtract to find how much pressure is lost.
$$\text{decrease} = 11.3 - 4.7 = 6.6 \text{ kPa}$$

**Turn the drop into a percentage decrease**

Divide the drop by the starting value and multiply by 100.
$$\text{percentage decrease} = \frac{6.6}{11.3} \times 100 \approx 58.4\%$$
This rounds to about 58%, so B is correct.

options.A: 42% is the percentage that remains (4.7 divided by 11.3 x 100), not the percentage lost. A classic mix-up.
options.B: Correct. A drop of 6.6 kPa from a starting 11.3 kPa is (6.6 / 11.3) x 100, about 58%.
options.C: 142% comes from dividing by the wrong number (the final 4.7 kPa instead of the starting 11.3 kPa). Percentage decrease must use the starting value.
options.D: 240% is just the ratio 11.3 divided by 4.7 x 100. It tells you how many times bigger the start is, not the percentage decrease.
